rules.body:
AKW-100 governs the wording of Keynotes and General Notes on
architectural construction drawings.
rules.title: AKW-100 governs the wording of Keynotes and General Notes on architectural construction drawings.

rules.body:
AKW-100 does not govern specification sections, schedules, sheet
titles, dimensions, or drawing labels.
rules.title: AKW-100 does not govern specification sections, schedules, sheet titles, dimensions, or drawing labels.

rules.body:
A Keynote is a contract document. Where a Keynote conflicts with
another contract document, remove the conflict. Do not rely on an order of
precedence to settle it.
rules.title: A Keynote is a contract document

rules.body:
AKW-100 conforms to the U.S. National CAD Standard, Uniform Drawing
System, Module 07 *Notations*, which governs format. AKW-100 governs wording.
Where the two appear to conflict, NCS wins on format and AKW-100 wins on
wording.
rules.title: AKW-100 conforms to the U.S. National CAD Standard, Uniform Drawing System, Module 07 *Notations*, which governs format

rules.body:
Terms used in this standard are defined in `CONTEXT.md`. Use the
canonical term. Terms listed under `_Avoid_` are not permitted in a Keynote or
in this standard.
rules.title: Terms used in this standard are defined in `CONTEXT.md`

rules.body: A rule is cited as `AKW-<area>.<number>`. Example: `AKW-40.3`.
rules.title: A rule is cited as `AKW-<area>.<number>`

rules.body:
A rule ID is never renumbered and never reused. A rule leaves the
standard in one of two ways, and either way it is recorded in
[`rules/90-archive.md`](./90-archive.md)

A stable ID means a review comment written today still resolves in five years.
rules.title: A rule ID is never renumbered and never reused

rules.body:
Until AKW-100 is first issued, rule IDs may be reorganised freely
and nothing is archived. **At first issue, IDs freeze.**
rules.title: Until AKW-100 is first issued, rule IDs may be reorganised freely and nothing is archived

rules.body:
A Keynote Number has this form:

```
[Phase Prefix][Discipline Prefix][1-99][Variant Letter]
```

Example: `D3A`, demolition, note 3, variant A.
Example: `DE3`, demolition, electrical, note 3.
Example: `E3`, proposed electrical, note 3.

Only the number is always present.
rules.title: A Keynote Number has this form

check.text: Form is `[phase][discipline][1-99][letter]`

rules.body:
The Phase Prefix separates work to be taken out from work to be
built:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `D` | Demolition |
| *(none)* | Proposed work |

The Phase Prefix is **mandatory** on every Keynote in any set that contains both
demolition and proposed work. It is not optional and it is not a discipline. A
contractor who confuses a demolition note with a proposed note removes something
you meant to keep.
rules.title: The Phase Prefix separates work to be taken out from work to be built

check.text: Phase Prefix `D` present on demolition notes wherever the set holds both demolition and proposed work

rules.body:
The Discipline Prefix names the trade:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `A` | Architectural |
| `P` | Plumbing and sprinkler |
| `E` | Electrical |
| `M` | Mechanical |
| `S` | Structural |
rules.title: The Discipline Prefix names the trade

check.text: Discipline Prefix matches the trade it names

rules.body:
The project decides whether to use a Discipline Prefix. A small
scope may drop it. If dropped, it is dropped on every Keynote in the set, not
some of them.

The Discipline Prefix becomes **mandatory** when any series would run past 99.
The range is 1 to 99 **per series**, so splitting by discipline gives you 99
numbers in each. Never continue a series past 99 and never invent a three-digit
number.
rules.title: The project decides whether to use a Discipline Prefix

check.text: Discipline Prefix used if any series would pass 99

rules.body:
A General Note uses the prefix `G` and takes no Phase Prefix and no
Discipline Prefix. `G` is reserved and is never used as a discipline.
rules.title: A General Note uses the prefix `G` and takes no Phase Prefix and no Discipline Prefix

check.text: A General Note is `G` with no Phase Prefix and no Discipline Prefix

rules.body:
A Keynote Number never contains a period. `3.1` reads as `31` at
plot scale. The period is too small to survive printing, scanning, and copying.
rules.title: A Keynote Number never contains a period

check.text: No period anywhere in the number

rules.body:
The parent number runs from 1 to 99. Variant letters run from `A`
upward, uppercase, and always follow the parent number so the family groups
visually.
rules.title: The parent number runs from 1 to 99

check.text: Variant letters run uppercase from `A`, immediately after the parent number

rules.body:
The letters `I` and `O` are banned. `I` misreads as `1` and `O`
misreads as `0` next to a number. Each is kept as a Reserved Keynote:

```
2I   INTENTIONALLY OMITTED
```
rules.title: The letters `I` and `O` are banned

check.text: No `I` or `O` variant letter

rules.body:
No number or letter is skipped silently. Any gap in a sequence is
printed as `INTENTIONALLY OMITTED`. A silent gap reads as a lost note, and the
contractor will ask, or worse, assume.
rules.title: No number or letter is skipped silently

check.text: Every gap in the sequence printed as `INTENTIONALLY OMITTED`

rules.body:
Keynote Numbers belong to the project, not to AKW-100. The same
number means different work on a different job. Reusing a project's numbering
convention across jobs is good practice, not a requirement.

**Within one project, after a set is issued**, a Keynote Number is never
reassigned to different work. Archive it as a Reserved Keynote instead. A
contractor holding an old bulletin must not read new work under an old number.
rules.title: Keynote Numbers belong to the project, not to AKW-100

check.text: After a set is issued, a number is never reassigned to different work

rules.body:
Every Parent Keynote is one of two types:

- **Complete**: the Parent is a full requirement and stands alone.
- **Stem**: the Parent is an opening that its Variants finish.
rules.title: Every Parent Keynote is one of two types

check.text: Parent type declared: **Complete** or **Stem**

rules.body:
A Complete Parent reads as a whole requirement with no Variant
present. Its Variants add a case; they do not change what the Parent already
requires.
rules.title: A Complete Parent reads as a whole requirement with no Variant present

check.text: A Variant adds a case; it does not change what the Parent requires

rules.body:
A Stem ends with a colon. Each Variant must form a grammatical
sentence when joined to the Stem. A Stem whose Variants are tagged
dispositions ends `AS TAGGED...` instead (AKW-20.11).

```
2    A LICENSED ELECTRICIAN, UNDER A SEPARATE PERMIT, IS RESPONSIBLE FOR:
2A     REDISTRIBUTION OF EXISTING LIGHTING (SEE RCP)
```
rules.title: A Stem ends with a colon

check.text: A Stem ends with a colon and each Variant completes it grammatically

rules.body:
A Stem prints in the Keynote Legend directly above its Variants,
indented one level. A Variant is never printed away from its Stem.
rules.title: A Stem prints in the Keynote Legend directly above its Variants, indented one level

rules.body:
A Variant never contradicts its Parent. **If it does, the Parent is
carrying too much.** Move the contested requirement down into the Variants and
the Parent becomes a Stem.

Before. `D3A` cancels `D3`:

```
D3    REMOVE FIXTURE. CAP AND REMOVE BACK TO THE SOURCE PANEL.
D3A   RETAIN AND RELOCATE EMERGENCY LIGHTING PER RCP.
```

After. The contested requirement moved down. The base keeps only what every
Variant performs:

```
D3    REMOVE EXISTING LIGHTING FIXTURE OR RECEPTACLE FROM ITS EXISTING
      LOCATION. PATCH AND REPAIR ANY DAMAGE AND PROVIDE CODE-COMPLIANT
      FIRE-STOPPING AS NEEDED. AS TAGGED...
D3A     ...CAP AND REMOVE THE ASSOCIATED CIRCUITING BACK TO THE SOURCE
        PANEL, OR TO THE NEAREST JUNCTION BOX
D3B     ...RETAIN AND RELOCATE EMERGENCY LIGHTING WITH ITS CIRCUITING
        PER PROPOSED RCP, ALIGN HEIGHTS WITH EXISTING ADJACENT LIGHTING
```
rules.title: A Variant never contradicts its Parent

check.text: No Variant contradicts its Parent

rules.body:
`IN LIEU OF <parent number>,` is the only permitted override, and
only where the Keynote Legend has already been issued and renumbering would
break a bulletin or a filed set. It is not a substitute for AKW-20.5.
rules.title: `IN LIEU OF <parent number>,` is the only permitted override, and only where the Keynote Legend has already been issu...

check.text: `IN LIEU OF` appears only against an issued legend

rules.body:
A requirement is written once. Where it is needed again, reference
it, by Keynote Number, sheet, or schedule. Two copies of a requirement become
two different requirements at the first revision.
rules.title: A requirement is written once

check.text: The requirement is not already written in another Keynote

rules.body:
A General Note carries no Keynote Tag and applies to the whole
sheet or set. It uses the prefix `G`. Because it has no tag, a General Note
**may** state its own Extent. This is the only exception to AKW-40.1. Every
other rule in AKW-100 applies to it unchanged.
rules.title: A General Note carries no Keynote Tag and applies to the whole sheet or set

check.text: States no Extent, unless it is a General Note

rules.body:
Every sentence in a Stem's text is performed at every location
where any of its Variants is tagged. Where a Variant would not perform a
sentence in the Stem - it retains what the Stem removes, or reuses what the
Stem discards - the base carries contested work. Move that sentence into the
affected Variants, or out into a separate Complete Keynote tagged at the same
location, before the set is issued.
rules.title: Every sentence in a Stem's text is performed at every location where any of its Variants is tagged

check.text: No sentence in a Stem's text is left unperformed by any of its Variants

rules.body:
Every set carrying Variant Keynotes carries a General Note
stating the inclusion:

```
G1   WHERE A LOCATION IS TAGGED BY MORE THAN ONE KEYNOTE TAG, THE FULL
     REQUIREMENT OF EVERY TAG APPLIES AT THAT LOCATION. A LETTERED VARIANT
     KEYNOTE INCLUDES THE FULL TEXT OF ITS PARENT KEYNOTE.
```

The printed note is the only text a takeoff is certain to carry. The rules
above govern the writing; this one binds the bid.
rules.title: Every set carrying Variant Keynotes carries a General Note stating the inclusion

check.text: A General Note states the inclusion where the set carries Variant Keynotes

rules.body:
Where a Stem's Variants are tagged dispositions, the Stem ends
`AS TAGGED...` and every Variant is prefixed `...`. The ellipsis is the
continuation signal: the Variant is part of the Stem's text. A Stem whose
Variants complete its sentence ends with a colon and no ellipsis
(AKW-20.3). The ellipsis is a printed flag, not a contract; the General Note
per AKW-20.10 binds.
rules.title: Where a Stem's Variants are tagged dispositions, the Stem ends `AS TAGGED...` and every Variant is prefixed `...`

check.text: A Stem with tagged dispositions ends `AS TAGGED...` and every Variant begins `...`

rules.body: A sentence has 25 words maximum.
rules.title: A sentence has 25 words maximum.

check.text: No sentence over 25 words

rules.body:
A Keynote has 5 sentences and 80 words maximum. A Parent and each
Variant are counted separately.
rules.title: A Keynote has 5 sentences and 80 words maximum

check.text: Not over 5 sentences or 80 words

rules.body:
Over either cap, split the Keynote into a Parent and Variants. The
caps exist to force that split. A note that will not fit is a note doing two
jobs.
rules.title: Over either cap, split the Keynote into a Parent and Variants

check.text: Over a cap, the Keynote is split, not trimmed

rules.body:
Write in the active voice, as an imperative.

- Write: `CLEAN, PATCH, AND REPAIR ALL PARTITIONS.`
- Not: `ALL PARTITIONS SHALL BE CLEANED, PATCHED, AND REPAIRED.`
rules.title: Write in the active voice, as an imperative

check.text: Active voice, imperative

rules.body:
One idea per sentence. A comma splice is a defect. Two independent
clauses joined by a comma become two sentences.

- Defect: `VENDOR SHALL VERIFY ALL CONDITIONS, IF SCOPE REQUIRES RELOCATION...`
- Fixed: `VENDOR SHALL VERIFY ALL CONDITIONS. IF SCOPE REQUIRES RELOCATION...`
rules.title: One idea per sentence

check.text: No comma splice

rules.body:
The default Actor is the general contractor, declared once in a
General Note. A Keynote names an Actor **only** when the work is not the general
contractor's: a separate-permit trade, a vendor, an owner-supplied installer.

Naming the general contractor on some notes and not others invites the question
of who performs the unnamed ones.
rules.title: The default Actor is the general contractor, declared once in a General Note

check.text: An Actor is named only where the work is not the general contractor's

rules.body:
`SHALL` states a condition the finished work must hold. The
imperative states an action to perform. Prefer the imperative.

- Action: `REPAINT ALL SURFACES TO MATCH EXISTING IN KIND.`
- Condition: `A RISE OVER 3 IN. SHALL BE RAMPED, NOT STEEPER THAN 1:12.`
rules.title: `SHALL` states a condition the finished work must hold

check.text: `SHALL` marks a condition the finished work must hold; an action takes the imperative

rules.body:
Do not open a Keynote with a courtesy or a hedge. No `PLEASE NOTE`,
`IT IS INTENDED THAT`, `THE CONTRACTOR IS ADVISED`. Start with the verb or the
subject of the work.
rules.title: Do not open a Keynote with a courtesy or a hedge

check.text: No courtesy or hedge opener

rules.body:
A Keynote states **what** work is required and **what end
condition** the work must be left in.

It does not state **means and methods**: the contractor's sequence, technique,
equipment, labour, or safety.

It does not state **Extent**: where the work is or how much of it there is. The
Keynote Tag carries Extent. Holding Extent out of the words is what makes one
Keynote serve every location.

Naming a **termination point** or a **physical end state** is scope, not method:

```
CAP AND REMOVE BACK TO THE SOURCE PANEL, OR TO THE NEAREST JUNCTION BOX
```

That fixes where the work stops. How the conductor is pulled stays the
electrician's business.
rules.title: A Keynote states **what** work is required and **what end condition** the work must be left in

check.text: States what work and what end condition

rules.body:
Vagueness about Extent is permitted **only** when something else
decides it: a stated trigger, or a Reference Document.

| Phrase | Verdict | Decider |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `AS SCHEDULED` | Pass | The schedule |
| `PER PROPOSED RCP` | Pass | The RCP |
| `IN KIND` | Pass | The existing product |
| `TYPICAL, U.O.N.` | Pass | The notes that say otherwise |
| `AS NEEDED IF THE CONDITION UNCOVERS A VOID` | Pass | The stated trigger |
| `AS NEEDED` (bare) | **Fail** | Nothing |
| `AS REQUIRED` (bare) | **Fail** | Nothing |
| `WHERE INDICATED` (bare) | **Fail** | Nothing |
rules.title: Vagueness about Extent is permitted **only** when something else decides it

check.text: Every vague Extent phrase has a trigger or a Reference Document

rules.body:
Vagueness about the **end condition** is banned outright. No
decider can rescue it, because the end condition is what the Keynote exists to
fix.

Banned words and phrases:

```
MAKE GOOD        MINOR          ADEQUATE       PROPER
SUITABLE         REASONABLE     NEAT           WORKMANLIKE
AS APPROPRIATE   TO SUIT        GOOD CONDITION ACCEPTABLE
```

Replace the adjective with the condition:

- Defect: `MAKE MINOR REPAIRS TO THE HANDRAILS.`
- Fixed: `REPAIR TO A SOUND SURFACE, FREE OF FLAKING COATING, RUST, AND
  CORROSION, READY FOR COATING.`

The condition sets the limit of work. An adjective never does.
rules.title: Vagueness about the **end condition** is banned outright

check.text: No banned end-condition word

rules.body:
`NOT LIMITED TO` widens scope in the contractor's favour, not
yours. It is banned unless widening is the deliberate intent, and then the
Keynote must also state the end condition that closes it.
rules.title: `NOT LIMITED TO` widens scope in the contractor's favour, not yours

check.text: No `NOT LIMITED TO` without a closing end condition

rules.body:
State a slope limit as `NOT STEEPER THAN 1:8` or `NOT FLATTER THAN
1:48`. `MIN.` and `MAX.` are banned next to a ratio.

A slope ratio inverts: a bigger second number means a gentler slope. `MINIMUM
SLOPE OF 1:8` reads to a contractor as permission to build 1:6, and they are
reading it correctly.

`MIN.` and `MAX.` remain legal with a plain dimension: `3 IN. MIN.`
rules.title: State a slope limit as `NOT STEEPER THAN 1:8` or `NOT FLATTER THAN 1:48`

check.text: Slope limits read `NOT STEEPER THAN` / `NOT FLATTER THAN`

rules.body:
Use `DAMAGE`, never `DAMAGES`. In a contract document *damages*
means money awarded in a lawsuit.
rules.title: Use `DAMAGE`, never `DAMAGES`

check.text: `DAMAGE`, not `DAMAGES`

rules.body:
Write `AND`. The ampersand `&` is not a word and is easy to lose at
plot scale.
rules.title: Write `AND`

check.text: No `&`

rules.body:
A slash `/` means **or**. It is permitted only where either reading
is acceptable. Where both items are required, write `AND`.

- `ALTER/AFFECT`: either reading is acceptable. Pass.
- `POWER/LOW-VOLTAGE`: both are required. **Fail.** Write `POWER AND
  LOW-VOLTAGE`.
rules.title: A slash `/` means **or**

check.text: Every `/` is a true "or"

rules.body:
Do not abbreviate a verb. `PREP` becomes `PREPARE`. Abbreviate
units only, per AKW-50.2.
rules.title: Do not abbreviate a verb

check.text: No abbreviated verbs

rules.body:
Name the thing precisely. `FLOORS` is not `FLOOR FINISHES`. `TRIM`
is not `CORNER GUARDS, WALL PROTECTION, AND BASE MOLDING`. A subcontractor
prices the cheapest defensible reading of the word you wrote.
rules.title: Name the thing precisely

check.text: Named precisely: `FLOOR FINISHES`, not `FLOORS`

rules.body:
One term per concept, across the whole set. The canonical terms
are in `CONTEXT.md`. Do not vary a term for style.
rules.title: One term per concept, across the whole set

check.text: Canonical terms from `CONTEXT.md`

rules.body: Keynote text is ALL CAPS.
rules.title: Keynote text is ALL CAPS.

check.text: ALL CAPS

rules.body:
Abbreviate units. Put one space between the number and the unit.

```
3 IN.        1/4 IN.        10 MM        8 FT.
```
rules.title: Abbreviate units

check.text: Units abbreviated, space before the unit

rules.body:
Never use the inch mark `"` or the foot mark `'`. They are lost in
CAD fonts, in scanned sets, and in PDF text search, and they collide with quote
marks.
rules.title: Never use the inch mark `"` or the foot mark `'`

check.text: No inch or foot marks

rules.body:
Default to imperial units. Where the prompt or the project is
metric, follow it. Do not convert a unit that belongs to a product's own name:
`10 MM RUBBER FLOORING` stays as the manufacturer sells it.
rules.title: Default to imperial units

check.text: Imperial units, unless the prompt or a product name is metric

rules.body: Underline a product called out by name.
rules.title: Underline a product called out by name.

check.text: Named products underlined

rules.body: Write a ratio as `1:12`. No spaces, no word "to".
rules.title: Write a ratio as `1:12`

check.text: Ratio written `1:12` — no space, no "to"

rules.body:
Do not use quote marks for emphasis. In a Keynote a quote mark
reads as an inch mark.

- Defect: `REMOVE EXISTING ELECTRICAL 'FIXTURE' OR 'OUTLET'`
- Fixed: `REMOVE EXISTING LIGHTING FIXTURE OR RECEPTACLE`
rules.title: Do not use quote marks for emphasis

check.text: No quote marks for emphasis

rules.body:
Write a fraction as `1/4`, not a decimal and not a typographic
fraction glyph.
rules.title: Write a fraction as `1/4`, not a decimal and not a typographic fraction glyph.

check.text: Fraction written `1/4`, not a decimal, not a fraction glyph

rules.body:
A parenthesis must close. An unbalanced parenthesis in an issued
Keynote is a defect, not a typo, because the reader cannot tell where the aside
was meant to end.
rules.title: A parenthesis must close

check.text: Parentheses balanced

rules.body:
Every Keynote meets the governing code at minimum. Code compliance
is the floor, not the requirement.
rules.title: Every Keynote meets the governing code at minimum

check.text: Meets the governing code at minimum

rules.body:
Recite a code value **only** when reciting it makes the requirement
measurable in the field. Otherwise cite the section and let the code govern.

- Recite: `A RISE OVER 1/4 IN. AND UP TO 1/2 IN. SHALL BE BEVELED, NOT STEEPER
  THAN 1:2.`: an inspector can measure this.
- Cite: `SEE ADA COMPLIANCE SHEET.`: the whole section does not fit in a note.
- Defect: `ALL TRANSITIONS TO BE ADA COMPLIANT.`: no threshold, no citation.
  This moves the entire code lookup onto the contractor and leaves you no ground
  to reject the work.
rules.title: Recite a code value **only** when reciting it makes the requirement measurable in the field

check.text: A recited value is measurable in the field

rules.body:
A recited value carries the condition that makes it legal. A value
stripped of its qualifying condition becomes a permission you did not intend.

```
2C   OVER 1/2 IN. TO 3 IN.: RAMPED, NOT STEEPER THAN 1:8, IN EXISTING
     CONSTRUCTION WHERE SPACE LIMITS REQUIRE
```

ADA §405.2 permits 1:8 only in existing construction, only where space limits
prohibit 1:12, and only up to a 3 in. rise. Drop those conditions and the
Keynote permits 1:8 in new construction, which the code does not.
rules.title: A recited value carries the condition that makes it legal

check.text: A recited value carries its qualifying condition

rules.body: Cite as `<CODE> §<SECTION>`. Example: `ADA §303`.
rules.title: Cite as `<CODE> §<SECTION>`

check.text: Cited as `<CODE> §<SECTION>`

rules.body:
Stricter than code is permitted. Looser is never permitted. Where a
Keynote is deliberately stricter, it is still stated as a requirement, not as a
preference.
rules.title: Stricter than code is permitted

check.text: Nothing is looser than code

rules.body:
Naming the local agency is permitted where it directs a filing or
an inspection: `DOB ELECTRICAL CONTROL UNIT`. Where the Keynote does not depend
on a specific agency, write `AUTHORITY HAVING JURISDICTION`.
rules.title: Naming the local agency is permitted where it directs a filing or an inspection

check.text: Agency named only where it directs a filing, else `AUTHORITY HAVING JURISDICTION`

rules.body:
A recited code value is verified by a person before the set is
issued. An agent may draft it; an agent does not confirm it. Every recited value
is flagged for that check.
rules.title: A recited code value is verified by a person before the set is issued

check.text: Every recited value flagged for human verification
